findings.title: Test helpers annotated `-> object` break strict pyright
findings.description: `failing_reconnect_patch()` returns `object`, and so do `scripted_session` (conftest.py:196), `typed_config` (conftest.py:218), and the `sdk_*` builders (conftest.py:96-150). Callers then use the results as context managers or read attributes from them: `with failing_reconnect_patch():` at tests/pipeline/actions/test_compact.py:262, tests/pipeline/actions/test_summary.py:1061 and :1086, and tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py:829. Also `with failing_reconnect_patch() as fresh_ctor:` and `fresh_ctor.return_value.query` at tests/pipeline/test_executor_each.py:288 and :305. Pyright strict reports the `with` on `object` and the attribute access on `object` as errors. `pyproject.toml` puts `tests` under strict checking, and the project rules make zero pyright errors a merge blocker. The same `object` return type is why the new tests carry many `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments. Return the real types (the type `patch()` returns, `SDKExecutionSession`, the SDK message classes) and drop the ignores.

findings.title: `set_model` is not gated by the unusable check
findings.description: The comment at sdk_session.py:125-126 says that after a failed reconnect "every later call then raises". The check is only in `dispatch`, `compact`, and `seed_context`. `set_model` is not gated. `_reconnect` resets `current_model` to `None` (sdk_session.py:427), so `set_model` always reaches `self.client`, which after a failed connect is the unconnected client built at sdk_session.py:426. `_dispatch_via_session` calls `session.set_model(model_id)` before `dispatch()` (src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:353). So the first call after a failed reconnect hits the dead client, and the error the user sees is whatever that call raises, not the "SDK session unusable" reason. The batch test `test_items_after_failed_reconnect_are_flagged_unusable` asserts that reason for item 2 and passes only because `ScriptedClient.set_model` is an `AsyncMock` that never fails (tests/pipeline/conftest.py:176). Gate `set_model` the same way and make the fake fail when disconnected. What the SDK raises for an unconnected `set_model` could not be checked here.

findings.title: `background_tasks_stopped` counts attempts, not successful stops
findings.description: `_stop_background` logs and continues when `stop_task` fails (sdk_session.py:336-341). It then sets `self.background_tasks_stopped = len(ids)` (line 344) and logs every description as "stopped" (lines 345-349). A failed stop is therefore reported as stopped in the step metadata (dispatch.py:369) and in the WARNING, even though the agent may still be running. The test `test_stop_task_failure_is_logged_and_next_id_still_stopped` (tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py, `TestBackgroundIdleTimeout`) checks the ERROR log and the call order, but not the count. Count only successful stops and name only those in the WARNING, or report failures separately.

findings.title: Synchronous config reads run on the event loop in async functions
findings.description: `_background_idle_timeout_s` is called from the async `_collect_turns` (sdk_session.py:224) and calls `get_typed_config`, which reads TOML synchronously. The same pattern appears in the async `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` (dispatch.py:142-153) and the async `open_pipeline_session` (sdk_session.py:455-461). `python.md` requires synchronous code in an async function to run in under 1 ms worst case. This can be exceeded: `_config_dir()` (src/squadron/config/manager.py:24-32) can run `shutil.copytree` on first use after a config migration. The steady-state cost is small, but the rule is explicit and these are new call sites. Read the config at a synchronous boundary, or move the read to `asyncio.to_thread`.

findings.title: Pipeline settings policy is duplicated, with config keys repeated as literals
findings.description: The same policy is computed in two places: `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` (dispatch.py:142-153) and `open_pipeline_session` (sdk_session.py:455-461). Both call `pipeline_setting_sources(include_user=get_typed_config("pipeline.user_settings", ...))` and `get_typed_config("pipeline.auto_memory", ...)`. Each key string appears in both places, and the project rules say lookup values are defined once. Move the policy into one helper, for example in `providers/sdk/settings.py`, that takes the cwd and returns both values, and call it from both paths.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` is 473 lines, and the session class also does turn collection
findings.description: The file is 473 lines against the roughly 300-line guideline. `SDKExecutionSession` now covers lifecycle (connect, reconnect, seeding), turn collection (`_collect_turns`, `_read_turn_with_retry`, `_read_turn`), the idle-timeout stop (`_stop_background`), and settings policy. `DispatchTurns` was already split into `sdk_turns.py`, but that module is documented as having "no client, no I/O", so the client-bound loop cannot move there without breaking that contract. A sibling module that takes the client as a parameter would keep the session class to lifecycle.

findings.title: No load-tier test for the new wait and idle-timeout path
findings.description: `python.md` requires at least one `tests/load/` test for code on concurrency or network paths, asserting latency, throughput, or resource bounds, and requires CI to gate it. The background-wait loop with per-message `asyncio.timeout`, the idle stop, and the leftover-turn discard fit that description. `tests/load/` contains `test_grep_timeout.py` and `test_worktree_concurrency.py`, and nothing for this slice. Earlier reviews under `project-documents/user/reviews/` waived load tests when the design stated no NFR, and this slice's design states none, so the PM may decide this is a waiver. Either add a load test or record the waiver.

findings.title: Dead `base_env` argument in the provider
findings.description: `kwargs` never receives an `env` key before this call; the only write is line 88. So `base_env=kwargs.get("env")` is always `None`, and the `# type: ignore[arg-type]` exists only to satisfy the type of that lookup. Remove the argument, or pass it only when a caller supplies one.

findings.title: `background_idle_timeout_s` accepts zero and negative values
findings.description: `get_typed_config` checks only that the value is an int. With `0` or a negative value, `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` fires immediately, so the first wait after the dispatch's own result stops every tracked agent. The key's description promises "seconds of silence". A `> 0` bound at the config layer would make the constraint explicit.

findings.title: Settings sources typed as `list[str]`, with the mismatch suppressed
findings.description: `SdkSettings.setting_sources` is `list[str]`, and the caller suppresses the mismatch against `ClaudeAgentOptions` with `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` (src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:466). If the SDK exposes a `Literal` source type in 0.2.160, the TypedDict should use it so the ignore can go. Not verified, because the SDK source is not available here.

findings.title: `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` is 115 lines
findings.description: The function runs from line 88 to line 202, well over the roughly 50-line guideline. Most of that length predates this diff, but the diff adds the settings block and the telemetry seeding. The settings block (dispatch.py:142-153) is the natural extraction point, and it also resolves the duplication finding above.

findings.title: Resume seeding, restore framing, and the artifact-failure text
findings.description: Verified by reading. Resume seeding runs once. `_load_resume_seed` runs before the loop, a connected session is rotated immediately, and a lazily connected one receives the seed at connect and then `resume_seed = None` (executor.py:487-516). The restore path passes raw text, and framing happens once in `_seeded_options` (summary.py:154-155, sdk_session.py:91). The artifact-failure error gets the agent's final text appended once, in `DispatchArtifactAction.execute` (dispatch_artifact.py:145-150).

structured_findings.summary: Test helpers annotated `-> object` break strict pyright
`set_model` is not gated by the unusable check
Synchronous config reads run on the event loop in async functions
Pipeline settings policy is duplicated, with config keys repeated as literals
`sdk_session.py` is 473 lines, and the session class also does turn collection
No load-tier test for the new wait and idle-timeout path
Settings sources typed as `list[str]`, with the mismatch suppressed
Resume seeding, restore framing, and the artifact-failure text
